functional_annotation: Multi-subunit transmembrane enzyme maintaining electrochemical and pH gradients
justification: Midgut V-ATPase pumps protons across apical membranes to maintain luminal alkalization and drive secondary nutrient absorption. RNAi silencing abolishes proton transport, causing an immediate collapse of the luminal pH gradient, gut tissue degeneration, and severe osmotic paralysis. Swift disruption of midgut physiology induces rapid larval starvation and death, providing immediate protection against oil palm frond defoliation.

functional_annotation: Nuclear hormone receptor regulating gene transcription during molting and pupation
life_stage_relevance: Larval molting and pupal transition stages
justification: Heterodimerizes with Ultraspiracle upon binding 20-hydroxyecdysone to drive transcriptional cascades required for cuticular apolysis and ecdysis. Silencing g6653 blocks ecdysone signaling, triggering complete developmental arrest and trapped cuticle syndrome during molting. Halting larval transitions prevents progression into destructive late-stage instars, while arthropod specificity eliminates non-target mammalian safety risks.

functional_annotation: Ligand-gated cation channel mediating fast excitatory synaptic transmission in CNS
justification: Core postsynaptic ligand-gated ion channel subunit in the central nervous system that opens upon acetylcholine binding to drive fast excitatory neurotransmission. Silencing g21280 prevents functional channel assembly, blocking postsynaptic depolarization and causing central nervous uncoupling. The resulting neurotoxic paralysis halts larval locomotion and feeding instantly, protecting oil palm fronds from ongoing foliage damage.

functional_annotation: Intracellular calcium release channel in sarcoplasmic reticulum controlling muscle contraction
justification: Multi-pass transmembrane channel on sarcoplasmic reticulum membranes regulating calcium ion efflux required for muscle excitation-contraction coupling. RNAi knockdown depletes calcium channels, preventing Ca2+ release into the muscle cytoplasm during motor nerve firing. Uncoupling muscle signaling causes complete flaccid body paralysis and intestinal peristalsis failure, leading to swift starvation and high larval mortality.

functional_annotation: Phase I monooxygenase mediating oxidative metabolism of synthetic chemicals
justification: Phase I detoxification enzyme catalyzing NADPH-dependent oxidative metabolism of dietary plant toxins and synthetic pesticides. Silencing g4044 blocks monooxygenase activity, causing internal accumulation of ingested phytochemicals and severe oxidative stress. Suppressing this enzymatic defense acts as an RNAi synergist, breaking metabolic resistance and sensitizing feeding larvae to co-applied controls.

functional_annotation: Seven-transmembrane GPCR regulating biogenic amine stress signaling and locomotion
justification: Seven-transmembrane GPCR binding octopamine to activate adenylyl cyclase and elevate cAMP, regulating stress responses, locomotion, and visceral contraction. Knockdown blocks octopaminergic signaling, causing severe behavioral disorientation, lethargy, and visceral regulation failure. Loss of motor coordination and feeding drive leads to rapid larval starvation, while invertebrate specificity guarantees non-target safety.

functional_annotation: Inhibitory ligand-gated chloride ion channel mediating muscle/neuron hyperpolarization
justification: Invertebrate-specific ligand-gated channel mediating postsynaptic hyperpolarization and inhibitory neurotransmission across neuromuscular junctions. Silencing g21781 depletes inhibitory chloride channels, triggering unchecked postsynaptic over-excitation, spastic muscle firing, and loss of motor coordination. Severe spastic paralysis halts feeding immediately, and its complete absence in vertebrates offers extreme bio-safety.

functional_annotation: Phase II detoxifying enzyme conjugating reduced glutathione to xenobiotic substrates
justification: Phase II metabolic enzyme detoxifying xenobiotics and plant toxins via glutathione conjugation while metabolizing cytotoxic lipid peroxidation products. Silencing g16110 halts Phase II conjugation, resulting in internal toxin accumulation, unmitigated oxidative stress, and widespread cellular damage. Disabling GST detoxification breaks insecticide tolerance, acting as a potent RNAi synergist that sensitizes bagworms to crop defenses.

functional_annotation: Voltage-gated sodium ion channel driving axonal membrane depolarization & action potentials
justification: Multi-pass transmembrane channel driving rapid Na+ influx during axonal action potential propagation across central and motor nervous circuits. Knockdown depletes sodium channels on axonal membranes, blocking electrical nerve impulse conduction and triggering neurogenic shock. Complete motor nerve blockage causes immediate systemic paralysis and feeding cessation, preventing further oil palm canopy defoliation.

functional_annotation: ATP-dependent efflux transport protein facilitating cellular xenobiotic extrusion
justification: ATP-dependent transmembrane efflux pump actively extruding xenobiotics, synthetic pesticides, and plant allelochemicals across cell membranes. Silencing g4998 blocks active cellular transport, causing toxic intracellular accumulation of waste products and dietary toxins. Impairing cellular efflux overcomes multi-drug metabolic resistance, sensitizing larvae to co-applied controls and causing systemic physiological breakdown.
